title: Texas A&M passes first test vs. Arizona State, but did Sun Devils expose Aggies’ flaws?
author: Doug Haller
content:
Texas A&M took a half to find its footing against a plucky Arizona State squad Saturday afternoon. But with the Sun Devils more than willing to keep handing the 10th-ranked Aggies opportunities, that didn’t end up being much of a problem.

The Aggies turned four turnovers into 24 points, including defensive end Marco Jones’ 55-yard pick six that sealed the deal in the fourth quarter, and Texas A&M ran away with a 48-20 victory in front of 107,523 at Kyle Field.

The Aggies came into the game as 14.5-point favorites, and it appeared they might have trouble covering as ASU and quarterback Cutter Boley moved the ball efficiently through three quarters. An Aggies offense that piled up 505 yards (236 rushing) on Missouri State last week had just six first downs in the first half while averaging just 3.1 yards per carry.

That all turned after Texas A&M forced an ASU three-and-out while holding onto a four-point lead near the end of the third quarter. The Aggies got the stop, then rattled off 24 unanswered points in the fourth to move to 2-0 on the season and hand ASU (1-1) its first loss.

Here’s what we learned:

It wasn’t that Arizona State’s defense couldn’t stop Texas A&M’s offense, because it mostly did. Going into the fourth quarter, the Sun Devils were winning the total yardage battle, 310-180, and only trailed 24-20.

Then the Aggies opened the fourth with a 33-yard touchdown pass from Marcel Reed to a wide-open Mario Craver — the second touchdown pass ASU allowed via a busted coverage. It illustrated the larger point that ASU’s defense was solid, but this game was lost in the margins.

Many of ASU’s nine penalties for 62 yards (to Texas A&M’s one for 5 yards) came on third downs on either side of the ball.

Then there was a first-quarter muffed punt inside their own 10, and a failed fake punt on the Sun Devils’ side of the field in the second quarter. In the third, a successful fourth-down stop was overturned by an Arizona State defensive flag. In the fourth, Texas A&M’s punter fumbled the ball, giving ASU possession at the Aggie 34. The very next play, Boley got hit, popping the ball in the air, where it was intercepted and returned for a 55-yard touchdown to put A&M up 38-20. ASU turned the ball over in just one play on the ensuing drive as well.

“We got to clean up our errors if we want to win a game against a top-10 team on the road,” ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham said on the ESPN broadcast after the first quarter.

They didn’t, and even though the Sun Devils’ defense punched above its weight, this team won’t contend for a Big 12 title if it can’t find a way to get out of its own way. — Devon Henderson

Before Saturday, Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko sounded like he understood what he was in for against Arizona State. He knew the Sun Devils were explosive. He expressed great respect for Dillingham and said he had studied him as an offensive play caller. Fans tend to judge a team based on its helmet logo, Elko said, “but this will be a really big challenge for us to see where we’re at.”

Texas A&M passed, taking advantage of Arizona State mistakes and wearing the Sun Devils down. Reed might be underappreciated, as his head coach insists, but he made big plays. Whenever Arizona State threatened, Reed answered. The biggest play: his 33-yard touchdown pass to Mario Craver that gave Texas A&M a 31-20 lead early in the fourth quarter.

Reed threw for 163 yards and three touchdowns. His receivers should give defenses problems all season. In addition to Craver, Alabama transfer Isaiah Horton caught two touchdown passes against ASU. Then there was the defense. Texas A&M’s got better as the game unfolded, pressuring Boley, forcing him into two interceptions that were returned for touchdowns. — Doug Haller

Texas A&M did not look great; Arizona State actually outplayed the Aggies in the first half. But there was a major difference: Texas A&M did not beat itself. No quality is more important in September. The key is how quickly the Aggies can correct their mistakes.

They did not run the ball well in the first half. Defensively, the Aggies had no answer for Arizona State receiver Reed Harris, who found too many holes in the secondary. Long snapping was a problem, once leading to a botched punt attempt. Reed opened the second half by locking onto a receiver with a pass that was easily intercepted.

The Aggies were good enough in other areas — they went most of the contest without committing a penalty — that it did not cost them. But it will in SEC play.

For a program looking to make a second straight trip to the College Football Playoff — The Athletic’s projections had the Aggies at 21 percent after Saturday’s win — the bar is high. — Haller

Arizona State has found its new dynamic offensive duo. Despite mistakes derailing the upset bid, transfers Boley (Kentucky) and Harris (Boston College) lit up Kyle Field.

Boley completed 21 of 34 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns, the vast majority of which went to Harris, who hauled in nine receptions for 189 yards and both of Boley’s touchdowns. That included a 58-yard catch-and-run hookup in the third quarter.

It harkened back to images of the recently departed combination of Sam Leavitt and Jordyn Tyson. Together, Leavitt and Tyson formed one of the country’s most feared pairings, leading the Sun Devils to a 2024 Big 12 title and College Football Playoff appearance. Leavitt was named a second-team All-Big 12 quarterback in 2024, and Tyson was a third-team AP All-American in both 2024 and 2025.

Tyson was drafted with the No. 12 pick by the New Orleans Saints in the 2026 NFL Draft, and Leavitt is now playing for Lane Kiffin at LSU. Against Texas A&M, Boley and Harris appeared primed to take the mantle.

Still, Arizona State will have to find firepower elsewhere to complement the duo. Alongside Harris, Colorado transfer Omarion Miller was ranked No. 36 on The Athletic’s list of the most impactful transfers of 2026. He caught nine passes for only 29 yards Saturday but had multiple key drops.

If the Sun Devils can’t develop more offensive weapons, Boley-to-Harris could have a ceiling. — Henderson

The Aggies begin SEC play at 3:30 p.m. ET next Saturday with a home game against Kentucky, then they have a trip to No. 8 LSU a week later.

The Sun Devils head overseas to open Big 12 play with a game against Kansas at Wembley Stadium in London next Saturday. Kickoff is scheduled for noon ET.
